relations.subject: William Roxburgh
relations.evidence: He studied medicine at Edinburgh University and matriculated around 1771 or 1772... In 1776 he received his first doctorate (MD) from Edinburgh University.

relations.subject: William Roxburgh
relations.evidence: He studied surgery under Dr Alexander Monro

relations.subject: William Roxburgh
relations.evidence: and learnt botany under John Hope.

relations.subject: William Roxburgh
relations.evidence: He received a second doctorate (also MD) on 12 January 1790 from Marischal College in Aberdeen.

relations.subject: William Roxburgh
relations.evidence: replaced Patrick Russell as the Company Botanist in Madras in April 1789.

relations.subject: William Roxburgh
relations.evidence: From 1793, he and Andrew Ross established a garden at Corcondah, where they worked on sugarcane and indigo.

relations.subject: William Roxburgh
relations.evidence: invited by the government of Bengal, to take charge of the Calcutta Botanical gardens from Colonel Robert Kyd in 1793 as Superintendent of the Company garden at Sibpur near Calcutta.

relations.subject: Francis Buchanan-Hamilton
relations.evidence: He was succeeded by Francis Buchanan-Hamilton.

relations.subject: William Roxburgh
relations.evidence: He was created Keeper of the Royal Botanic Garden, Edinburgh on arrival until death.

relations.subject: William Carey
relations.evidence: In 1824, Carey edited and published vol. 2 of Roxburgh's Flora Indica, including extensive remarks and contributions by Dr. Nathaniel Wallich. Carey and Wallich continued to work in the field of botany
